newsitem.title: CHINA: China rewards tipoffs to catch video pirates.
newsitem.headline: China rewards tipoffs to catch video pirates.

text.p: A system of rewards for informers against compact disc pirates in China's southern Guangdong province has paid off, the Xinhua news agency said on Tuesday.

The provincial government announced last September that people who provided clues to catch intellectual property rights thieves would receive rewards, the agency quoted the China Culture News as saying.
Since then, police have destroyed two underground video compact disc production lines in the province, it said.
Those reporting shops involved in storing or marketing pornographic or pirate audio-video products would also receive rewards, it said.
Informers would receive police protection, it said.
However, underground factories still existed, posing a "hard nut" for the province in its anti-piracy drive, it said.
Provincial authorities closed one plant making pirated compact discs in September and a second in October and had paid informers rewards of 300,000 yuan ($36,100) each.
The campaign was part of a nationwide assault on pornographic and counterfeit goods, officials have said.
China and the United States narrowly averted a bruising trade war earlier this year over U.S. accusations that China was not doing enough to combat rampant piracy of intellectual property rights.
Booming Guangdong has been a hotbed for the illegal manufacture of compact discs, videotapes and tape cassettes.
